added.heading: You were added to {workspace}
added.reason: You got this email because a server admin of {site} added this address. If you didn't expect it, you can ignore it.
added.subject: You were added to {workspace} on {site}
added.text: {who} added you to {workspace} on {site} as {role}: answer and follow up on the calls its assistant takes.
addedNotice.reason: You got this email because a server admin of {site} added you. If you didn't expect it, tell the workspace's owner.
addedToWorkspace.note: The link works for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Enter this email address on the sign-in page and we send you a code.
addedToWorkspace.preheader: {inviter} added you as {role}. Sign in with this address to join.
adminAlert.adminGranted.subject: New instance admin on {brand}: {email}
adminAlert.billingReconcile.kind: {kind, select, missed_events {Events not received} events_truncated {Events not compared (more than the run reads)} failed_events {Events that keep failing} run_failed {The comparison could not run} status {Status} period {Billing period} quantity {Workspace seats} payment_method {Payment method} other {Other}}
adminAlert.billingReconcile.nightly: Events that were not received are processed now. The rest needs a look in Server admin and the Stripe Dashboard.
adminAlert.billingReconcile.subject: Billing on {brand} differs from Stripe: {count, plural, one {# finding} other {# findings}}
adminAlert.billingReconcile.text: The nightly comparison of the bills with Stripe found these differences:
adminAlert.billingSwitch.subject: Billing was turned {on, select, yes {on} other {off}}
adminAlert.billingSwitch.text: {actor} turned billing {on, select, yes {on, with the Stripe account {account} in {mode} mode: businesses on this install are charged} other {off: nothing is charged and no card is used}} (Server admin › Providers › Billing).
adminAlert.billingUnusable.fix: Run the migrations again, or fix the keys in Server admin › Providers › Billing. You get this email once; billing comes back on its own once it works.
adminAlert.billingUnusable.subject: Billing on {brand} is switched on but not working
adminAlert.billingUnusable.text: {reason, select, guards {The database rules that keep the billing ledger correct are missing, changed or could not be checked.} other {The Stripe keys are missing, or this server does not allow them.}} Until billing works again, calls of workspaces on a bill are refused and filed as missed.
adminAlert.cappedCall.check: Check the call in Server admin and with the carrier. If it really ran that long, credit or charge the difference by hand.
adminAlert.cappedCall.subject: A call on {brand} was billed less than it reported
adminAlert.cappedCall.text: A call reported {reported} seconds, more than its time limit plus the grace allows, so it was billed for {billed} seconds. A wrong duration, a stuck call or a call the stale sweep did not end can cause this.
adminAlert.checkAudit: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Audit log.
adminAlert.checkProviders: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Providers and Audit log.
adminAlert.checkUsers: If you did not expect this, sign in with your passkey and check Server admin › Users and Audit log.
adminAlert.enrolmentIssued.subject: Passkey enrolment code issued on {brand}: {email}
adminAlert.enrolmentIssued.text: {actor} issued a one-time code for the first passkey of {email}, an instance admin without a passkey. Nothing was removed and their sessions and AI agent setup links keep working.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.failed: The nightly billing check stopped with an error, so the ledger was not compared tonight. The server log has the error.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.failedSubject: The billing check on {brand} could not run
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.guards: Billing is off: the database rules that keep the ledger correct are missing, disabled or changed. Run the migrations again; billing comes back at the next good check.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.kind: {kind, select, balance {Balance} reserved {Reserved for running calls} counter_allowance {Included minutes used} counter_usage {Usage this period} uncredited {Recharge not credited} other {Other}}
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.nightly: The billing check runs every night; you get this email each night until it is fixed.
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.subject: Billing check on {brand}: {count, plural, one {# problem} other {# problems}} found
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.sums: These stored sums do not match the ledger (amounts in millionths of a dollar):
adminAlert.ledgerCheck.uncredited: Bill {bill}: recharge {recharge} is paid but the balance was not credited
adminAlert.passkeysReset.admin: They are an instance admin and got a new enrolment code for their first passkey.
adminAlert.passkeysReset.subject: Passkeys reset on {brand}: {email}
adminAlert.passkeysReset.text: {actor} removed every passkey of {email} ({count, plural, one {# removed} other {# removed}}) and ended their sessions and AI agent setup links.
adminAlert.providerFailure.impact: Calls or emails that need it may not work until it is fixed. Server admin › Providers shows the latest failure; a successful test or call clears it.
adminAlert.providerFailure.once: You get this email once per failure, not for every call.
adminAlert.providerFailure.subject: {provider} is failing on {brand}: {reason, select, quota {quota or credit used up} auth {key rejected} permission {missing permission} not_found {not found} config {setting refused} network {not reachable} timeout {no answer in time} no_output {answered with nothing} other {failing}}
adminAlert.reason: You got this email because you are a server admin of {site}. Every server admin gets these alerts.
adminAlert.rechargeNotCredited.next: Check the invoice in the Stripe Dashboard. If the customer really paid, credit the bill by hand for this recharge attempt (billing.credit with the recharge id), so it can never be credited twice; otherwise nothing needs to happen.
adminAlert.rechargeNotCredited.reason: {reason, select, out_of_band {Stripe shows the recharge invoice as paid, but it was marked paid outside Stripe.} not_charged {Stripe shows the recharge invoice as paid, but card payments do not cover its total (a customer credit balance or a partial payment).} discounted {The recharge invoice has a discount, so the card paid less than the recharge.} amount_mismatch {The recharge invoice's amount is not the amount of the recharge attempt.} no_line {The recharge invoice has no line for this recharge attempt.} currency {The recharge invoice is not in US dollars.} customer_mismatch {The recharge invoice belongs to another Stripe customer than the bill.} canceled {The recharge attempt was canceled, but its invoice was paid.} other {The recharge invoice did not pass the payment checks.}} Nothing was added to the balance.
adminAlert.rechargeNotCredited.subject: A paid recharge on {brand} was not credited
adminAlert.rechargeSetup.check: Check the Stripe keys and their permissions in Server admin › Providers › Billing, and the customer in the Stripe Dashboard.
adminAlert.rechargeSetup.subject: A recharge on {brand} failed on the Stripe setup
adminAlert.rechargeSetup.text: Stripe refused the recharge ({code}): the keys, their permissions or the customer are not right. The attempt was canceled and the bill owner was not told. Until this is fixed, every recharge fails the same way.
adminAlert.settings.agentEnds: That admin ends the link with End access on the setup page; disabling the admin ends it too.
adminAlert.settings.moneyText: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} other {changed the {provider} settings}} (Server admin › Providers). They control billing: charges, refunds and customers.
adminAlert.settings.moneyTextAgent: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} other {changed the {provider} settings}} through the AI agent setup link {prefix}…{hasMade, select, yes {, made {made}} other {}}. They control billing: charges, refunds and customers.
adminAlert.settings.subject: {change, select, changed {{provider} settings changed} removed {{provider} settings removed} switched {Email now sent with {provider}} other {Email provider pick cleared}}{agent, select, yes { by an AI agent} other {}}
adminAlert.settings.text: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} switched {switched email to {provider}} other {cleared which email provider sends}} (Server admin › Providers). They decide how people sign in or get sign-in codes.
adminAlert.settings.textAgent: {actor} {change, select, changed {changed the {provider} settings} removed {removed the {provider} settings} switched {switched email to {provider}} other {cleared which email provider sends}} through the AI agent setup link {prefix}…{hasMade, select, yes {, made {made}} other {}}. They decide how people sign in or get sign-in codes.
adminAlert.signIn.ifNot: If this was them, nothing to do. If not, someone has their passkey, authenticator app or device: sign in with your own passkey, then in Server admin › Users disable the account and reset its passkeys.
adminAlert.signIn.subject: Admin sign-in from a new device on {brand}: {who}
adminAlert.signIn.text: {method, select, passkey {{who}, a server admin, confirmed with their passkey from a device not seen before for them.} authenticator {{who}, a server admin, confirmed with their authenticator app from a device not seen before for them.} password {{who}, a server admin, signed in with a password from a device not seen before for them.} email_code {{who}, a server admin, signed in with an email code from a device not seen before for them.} email_link {{who}, a server admin, signed in with an email link from a device not seen before for them.} provider {{who}, a server admin, signed in with {provider} from a device not seen before for them.} unknown {{who}, a server admin, signed in with a sign-in method this server does not recognise from a device not seen before for them.} other {{who}, a server admin, signed in with “{how}” from a device not seen before for them.}}
adminAlert.stripeEventFailed.next: Fix the cause (Stripe keys, the ledger guards, an unknown period), then process it again with billing.reprocessEvent. It is applied once, however often it runs.
adminAlert.stripeEventFailed.subject: A Stripe event on {brand} could not be processed
adminAlert.stripeEventFailed.text: Billing tried to process this Stripe event {attempts} times and failed each time. Until it is processed, what it reports (a payment, a status change) is not applied to the bill.
adminAlert.stuckRecharges.check: Look the invoices up in Stripe (metadata billing_recharge_id) and the billing webhook's deliveries.
adminAlert.stuckRecharges.subject: {count, plural, one {# recharge} other {# recharges}} on {brand} still waiting to be settled
adminAlert.stuckRecharges.text: These recharge attempts have been pending for more than 2 hours. While one is pending, its bill gets no new automatic recharge, and once the balance runs out its calls are refused.
assigned.reason: You got this email because a teammate in {workspace} assigned you a call.
assigned.subject: {by} assigned you a call: {topic}
authenticatorChanged.heading: {change, select, added {An authenticator app was added} other {The authenticator app was removed}}
authenticatorChanged.notYou: If it wasn't you, ask another server admin of your {brand} to reset your passkeys (Server admin › Users, your name, Reset passkeys): that also removes the authenticator app. Then sign in and add your own again.
authenticatorChanged.subject: {change, select, added {An authenticator app was added to} other {The authenticator app was removed from}} your {brand} account
authenticatorChanged.text: {change, select, added {An authenticator app was added to your {brand} account at {site}. It opens Server admin like your passkey.} other {The authenticator app was removed from your {brand} account at {site}.}}
billing.capReached.effect: Calls go on until the balance is {buffer} below zero; then the assistant stops answering new calls. Buy minutes or raise the cap in Settings › Billing to keep it answering.
billing.capReached.subject: Your {brand} balance reached its monthly recharge cap
billing.capReached.text: Your prepaid balance was recharged up to its monthly cap of {cap}, so no more automatic recharges happen this month (UTC).
billing.lowBalance.effect: When the balance runs out, the assistant stops answering new calls. Buy minutes or turn auto-recharge on in Settings › Billing.
billing.lowBalance.subject: Your {brand} balance is low
billing.lowBalance.text: Your prepaid balance is down to {balance}, and auto-recharge is off.
billing.reason: You got this email because you pay for a bill on {site}.
billing.rechargeFailed.effect: Calls go on until the balance is {buffer} below zero; then the assistant stops answering new calls. No new recharge is tried until you update your card or retry it in Settings › Billing.
billing.rechargeFailed.subject: Your {brand} balance could not be recharged
billing.rechargeFailed.text: We tried to charge {amount} to your saved card to recharge your prepaid balance, and the payment did not go through.
booking.change: To change or cancel it, call {business} at {phone}.
booking.changeBack: To change or cancel it, call {business} back.
booking.heading: Your {what} is booked
booking.reason: You got this email because you booked by phone with {business} and gave this address.
booking.subject: Confirmed: your {what} with {business}, {when}
call.reason: You get one email per call to {workspace}.
call.recording: The recording and the transcript are in {brand}.
call.subject: {topic} · {from}
code.note: It works once and expires in {minutes} minutes. Don't share this code: nobody from {brand} or your team will ever ask you for it.
confirmationCode.heading: Your confirmation code
confirmationCode.note: It works once and expires in {minutes} minutes. Don't share this code with anyone; {brand} staff will never ask for it.
confirmationCode.preheader: It confirms this address for your {brand} account at {site}.
confirmationCode.reason: You got this email because your account asked to confirm this address. If it wasn't you, you can ignore it.
confirmationCode.subject: {code} is your {brand} confirmation code
confirmationCode.text: This code confirms this address for your {brand} account at {site}. Enter it on {site}, where {brand} asked for it.
emailChangeCode.heading: Confirm your new email address
emailChangeCode.preheader: Enter it in Account settings on {site} to sign in with this address from now on.
emailChangeCode.reason: You got this email because someone signed in to {brand} on {site} asked to use this address for their account. If it wasn't you, you can ignore it: nothing changes without this code.
emailChangeCode.subject: {code} is your {brand} code to change your email
emailChangeCode.text: Enter this code in Account settings on {site}. Your {brand} account then uses this address to sign in and for its emails.
emailChangeConfirm.heading: Confirm it's you
emailChangeConfirm.preheader: Someone signed in to your account on {site} wants to change its email address.
emailChangeConfirm.reason: You got this email because it is the address of your account. If it wasn't you, don't enter the code: change your password and tell your administrator.
emailChangeConfirm.subject: {code} is your {brand} code to confirm it's you
emailChangeConfirm.text: Someone signed in to your {brand} account on {site} wants to change its email address. Enter this code in Account settings to confirm it's you.
emailChangeRefused.heading: This address can't be used
emailChangeRefused.note: If that was you, use a different address, or sign in with this one instead. If it wasn't you, you can ignore this email.
emailChangeRefused.preheader: Someone asked to move their account to this address. Nothing was changed.
emailChangeRefused.reason: You got this email because this address was entered as a new sign-in address. We always send it.
emailChangeRefused.subject: This address can't be used for another {brand} account
emailChangeRefused.text: Someone signed in to {brand} on {site} asked to use this address for their account. It already belongs to an account there or is kept for a server admin, so it can't be used for another one, and nothing was changed.
emailChanged.heading: Your email address was changed
emailChanged.notYou: If it was not you, someone has access to your account: tell your administrator right away, so they can turn the account off.
emailChanged.preheader: Your account now signs in with {email}.
emailChanged.reason: You got this email because it was the address of your account until now. We always send it.
emailChanged.subject: The email of your {brand} account was changed
emailChanged.text: Your {brand} account at {site} now uses {email} to sign in and for its emails, and its other sessions were signed out. This address no longer signs in to it.
enterAddress: Enter this email address on the sign-in page and we send you a code.
firstCall.heading: Your first call
firstCall.reason: From now on you get one email per call to {workspace}.
firstCall.subject: Your first real call · {from}
firstCall.text: The first real call to {workspace} just came in.
firstCall.textTitle: The first real call to {workspace} just came in: {title}.
impersonationApiKey.heading: A server admin created an API key for you
impersonationApiKey.key: The key: {name} ({prefix}), with the {role, select, admin {Admin} other {Member}} role.
impersonationApiKey.limits: The key keeps working after the support access ends, until it is revoked. It is listed in Workspace settings › Developers with the admin's name, and everything done with it is in the audit log under their name.
impersonationApiKey.preheader: {by} created an API key while signed in as you on {when}.
impersonationApiKey.subject: A server admin created an API key in your {brand} account
impersonationApiKey.text: {by} created an API key while signed in as you at {site} on {when}{hasWorkspace, select, yes {, in the workspace {workspace}} other {}}.
impersonationApiKey.unexpected: If you do not need it, revoke it in Workspace settings › Developers. If you did not expect this, tell your administrator.
impersonationStarted.heading: A server admin signed in as you
impersonationStarted.limits: This access ends after {minutes} minutes at the latest. It cannot change your password, email address, passkeys or sign-in methods, and everything done in it is in the audit log under their name.
impersonationStarted.subject: A server admin signed in to your {brand} account
impersonationStarted.text: {by} signed in as you at {site} on {when}{hasWorkspace, select, yes {, in the workspace {workspace}} other {}}, to see {brand} as you do.
impersonationStarted.unexpected: If you did not expect this, tell your administrator.
impersonationStarted.why: You got this email because the server admins of {site} have turned on notices about support access.
installTest.heading: Your email works
installTest.preheader: Enter the code in the setup to finish the test. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
installTest.reason: You got this email because you tested email in the {brand} setup at {site}.
installTest.subject: {code} is your {brand} test code
installTest.text: Enter this code in the setup to finish the test:
invitation.note: The link works for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}. Sign in with this address ({email}): enter it on the sign-in page and we email you a code.
invitation.preheader: {inviter} invited you. The invitation is open for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
invitation.reason: You got this email because someone invited this address. If you didn't expect it, you can ignore it.
invitation.subject: Join {workspace} on {brand}
invitation.text: {inviter} invited you to join {workspace} on {brand} at {site}: answer and follow up on the calls its assistant takes.
memberAdded.check: If you didn't expect this, check the team and remove them there.
memberAdded.heading: {who} was added to {workspace}
memberAdded.pending: They join once they confirm their email address.
memberAdded.reason: You got this email because you own {workspace}, and a server admin of {site} changed its team. We always send it.
memberAdded.subject: {admin} added {who} to {workspace}
passkeyChanged.heading: {change, select, added {A passkey was added} other {A passkey was removed}}
passkeyChanged.notYou: If it wasn't you, ask a server admin of your {brand} to remove all passkeys of your account (Server admin › Users, your name, Reset passkeys), then sign in and add your own again.
passkeyChanged.subject: {change, select, added {A passkey was added to} other {A passkey was removed from}} your {brand} account
passkeyChanged.text: {change, select, added {A passkey was added to} other {A passkey was removed from}} your {brand} account at {site}.
passkeyEnrolment.next: Get the code from them, then add your passkey under Account settings › Sign-in & security.
passkeyEnrolment.preheader: Use it to add your first passkey. Nothing else changed.
passkeyEnrolment.text: {issuedBy} issued a one-time code for the first passkey of your {brand} account. Nothing was removed and you are still signed in.
passkeyEnrolment.unexpected: If you did not ask for this, tell the other administrators of {brand} at once: whoever has the code can add a passkey to your account.
passkeysReset.heading: {kind, select, removed {Your passkeys were removed} other {Passkey enrolment code issued}}
passkeysReset.next: Sign in with an email code or your password, then add a new passkey under Account settings › Sign-in & security.
passkeysReset.preheader: Sign in again, then add a new passkey.
passkeysReset.subject: {kind, select, removed {The passkeys of your {brand} account were removed} other {A passkey enrolment code was issued for your {brand} account}}
passkeysReset.text: {kind, select, removed {A server admin removed every passkey of your {brand} account and signed you out everywhere.} other {A server admin issued a passkey enrolment code for your {brand} account and signed you out everywhere.}}
passkeysReset.unexpected: If you did not ask for this, tell your administrator.
passwordChanged.heading: Your password was changed
passwordChanged.notYou: If it was not you, someone can read your email: secure your mailbox first, then use "Forgot password?" on the sign-in page to set a new password, and tell your administrator.
passwordChanged.subject: The password of your {brand} account was changed
passwordChanged.text: The password of your {brand} account at {site} was reset with a code sent to this address, and you were signed out everywhere.
passwordReset.heading: Reset your password
passwordReset.preheader: Enter it on the sign-in page of {site} to set a new password. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
passwordReset.reason: You got this email because someone asked to reset the password for this address on {site}. If it wasn't you, you can ignore it: your password stays the same.
passwordReset.subject: {code} is your {brand} password reset code
passwordReset.text: Enter this code on the {brand} sign-in page at {site}, then choose a new password.
push.title: {kind, select, urgent {Urgent call from {who}} message {Message from {who}} other {New call from {who}}}
role.inSentence: {role, select, owner {an owner} admin {an admin} other {a member}}
security.nothingToDo: If this was you, there is nothing to do.
security.reason: You got this email because the sign-in methods of your account changed. We always send it.
setup.day0HeadingCall: Try it with a real call
setup.day0Subject: {assistant} is almost ready to answer for {workspace}
setup.day0Text: {assistant} is set up for {workspace}. One thing is left before callers reach {assistant}:
setup.day1Subject: {assistant} hasn't answered a real call yet
setup.day3Subject: Still one step before {assistant} answers your calls
setup.nudgeText: No real calls have reached {assistant} yet. The one thing left:
setup.partner: Rather have someone do it for you? A partner can set up {brand} for {workspace}, phone settings included.
setup.reason: You get a few emails while {workspace} gets set up. They stop once {assistant} answers real calls.
setup.stepCallAll: Call your business number from a phone that isn't one of yours (a friend's): {assistant} answers.
setup.stepCallMissed: Call your business number from a phone that isn't one of yours (a friend's) and let it ring. When you don't pick up, {assistant} does.
setup.stepForwardAll: If you haven't yet, forward your business line to {to}. The steps for your phone company are in {brand}.
setup.stepForwardMissed: If you haven't yet, forward the calls you don't pick up on your business line to {to}. The steps for your phone company are in {brand}.
setup.stepNumber: Pick a phone number for {assistant}. It takes a minute in {brand}.
signInCode.heading: Your sign-in code
signInCode.linkPreheader: Click the button or enter the code on {site}. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
signInCode.linkText: Click the button to sign in to {brand} at {site}. It works in the browser where you asked for the code.
signInCode.orCode: Or enter this code on the sign-in page at {site}:
signInCode.preheader: Enter it on the sign-in page of {site}. It expires in {minutes} minutes.
signInCode.reason: You got this email because someone asked to sign in to {site} with this address. If it wasn't you, you can ignore it.
signInCode.subject: {code} is your {brand} sign-in code
signInCode.text: Enter this code on the {brand} sign-in page at {site}.
spendingCap.change: A server admin can change the cap in Server admin › Workspaces › {workspace}.
spendingCap.levelEffect: When it reaches the cap, the assistant stops answering calls until the end of the month (UTC): callers hear that the business will call them back, and each call shows up in the inbox as a missed call to return.
spendingCap.levelSubject: {workspace} used {percent} of its monthly spending cap
spendingCap.levelText: {workspace} used about {spent} of its monthly spending cap of {cap} ({percent}, estimated).
spendingCap.reachedEffect: Until the end of the month (UTC) the assistant no longer answers calls: callers hear that the business will call them back, and each call shows up in the inbox as a missed call with “Call back”. Test calls are off too.
spendingCap.reachedText: {workspace} reached its monthly spending cap of {cap} (estimated cost this month: about {spent}).
spendingCap.reason: You got this email because you own {workspace} or are a server admin of {site}.
unsubscribe.confirmText: You stop getting the emails that help set up {brand}. Call emails are not affected.
unsubscribe.doneText: You won’t get any more of them. Call emails are not affected.
unsubscribe.invalidText: Turn off setup emails in Account settings, Notifications after signing in instead.
week.heading: Your first week
week.preheader: {assistant} answered {count, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}} in the first week.
week.reason: You get this once, a week after {workspace} got its owner.
week.subject: {assistant}'s first week at {workspace}
week.text: In its first week, {assistant} answered {count, plural, one {# call} other {# calls}} for {workspace}.
welcome.heading: Welcome, {name}
welcome.preheader: Sign in at {site} with this address.
welcome.reason: You got this email because a server admin of {site} added you.
welcome.subject: Your {brand} account is ready
welcome.text: A server admin created a {brand} account for you at {site}.
workspaceDeleted.accountDeleted: Your {brand} account at {site} was deleted with it, because you belonged to no other workspace. You can't sign in there anymore.
workspaceDeleted.accountKept: Your account and your other workspaces stay as they are.
workspaceDeleted.heading: {workspace} was deleted
workspaceDeleted.reason: You got this email because you were a member of {workspace} on {site}. We always send it.
workspaceDeleted.subject: {workspace} was deleted on {brand}
workspaceDeleted.text: {by} deleted the workspace {workspace} on {when}. Its calls, contacts, recordings and settings are gone, and nobody can open it anymore.
workspaceDeleted.unexpected: If you didn't expect this, ask the workspace owner.
workspaceRemoved.accountDeleted: Your {brand} account at {site} was deleted too, because you belonged to no other workspace. You can't sign in there anymore.
workspaceRemoved.heading: You were removed from {workspace}

workspaceRemoved.text: {by} removed you from the workspace {workspace} on {when}. You no longer have access to its calls, contacts and settings.
workspaceRemoved.unexpected: If you didn't expect this, ask the workspace owner for a new invitation.
